stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Live preview across GO, UP, MX platforms is a complex feature requiring real-time rendering, iframe sandboxing, and state synchronization. Openspec needed to elaborate AC and technical depth; speckit needed to harden testability, security (iframe sandbox, XSS), and edge cases. Both assigned with openspec running first.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — Contentstack Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. Attachment points are useContent (hook consumed by 236+ components), ContentstackContext (provider), and contentstack service. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. All VCs stop at our side of the Contentstack boundary (mocked client).

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with valuable notes identifying attachment points (useContent hook consumed by 236+ components, ContentstackContext provider, contentstack service). Since openspec's AC list was empty, all criteria above are new. I derived them from the story title/description ('Live Preview of Content in CMS') and openspec's attachment-point analysis. Key areas covered: (1) core real-time update behavior (AC-1 through AC-3), (2) connection lifecycle and error resilience (AC-4, AC-5, AC-11), (3) rapid-update edge case (AC-6), (4) security/XSS prevention (AC-7, AC-13), (5) accessibility for dynamic content (AC-9), (6) opt-out and fallback paths (AC-8, AC-10), (7) malformed payload handling (AC-12). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I did not have access to the actual source files for useContent, ContentstackContext, or the contentstack service. The criteria are based on the story description alone and may need adjustment once those files are reviewed for existing patterns, error-handling conventions, and API surfaces.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents were assigned but the pipeline did not function as designed. Openspec was tasked with elaborating acceptance criteria for an empty-AC story but produced none (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0). It did provide valuable attachment-point analysis (useContent hook consumed by 236+ components, ContentstackContext provider, contentstack service), which is useful context. Speckit then had to author all ACs from scratch from the story title/description — this is outside speckit's review/hardening role and represents a process failure in the openspec step. Speckit's ACs appear reasonably structured (covering real-time updates, connection lifecycle, error resilience, rapid-update edge cases, XSS/security, accessibility, opt-out/fallback, malformed payload handling) but are explicitly unvalidated against the actual source files. Speckit notes it had no access to useContent, ContentstackContext, or contentstack service source code, so criteria may not align with existing codebase patterns, error-handling conventions, or API surfaces. Additionally, no story splits were proposed despite the feature spanning real-time rendering, iframe sandboxing, and state synchronization across three platforms (GO, UP, MX) — this likely warrants decomposition into smaller stories. The collaborative work is non-overlapping but only because openspec failed to deliver its primary output, forcing speckit into an authoring role it should not have held.
